small_guidance:
- The GEMM uses `allow_tf32=False` which forces full fp32 mma — switch to `allow_tf32=True` (inputs are fp32 from rand, loose tolerance 5e-2 easily covers TF32). This alone should give ~2-3x on the dominant op.
- Add larger tile configs sized for M=1024, N=8192, K=8192: `BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64` and `BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64` with `num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4`. Drop the small 64-tile configs that won't win at this shape.
- Cache `Bt` once in `__init__` (or first forward) instead of via the `data_ptr()==0` check which re-runs `.t().contiguous()` whenever the cache check fails; also register it as a buffer so it stays on device.
large_guidance:
- The GEMM dominates (~134 GFLOPs); rewrite it as a TF32 (or fp16-accumulate-fp32) tiled GEMM with a persistent / split-K-free design, using `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` and load B without transposing — use a `B^T` once-precomputed contiguous buffer so both A and B inner axes are contiguous loads of stride 1.
- Consider fusing the bias-add + the GroupNorm first-pass reduction (sum and sum-of-squares per group) into the GEMM epilogue when `BLOCK_N` aligns with `C_per_G=512`: each program writes its tile and atomically accumulates partial group sums, eliminating one full read of the 1024×8192 tensor.
- Alternatively, keep GEMM and GN separate but make the GN kernel process a full row (C=8192) per program with a 2D block over channels — BLOCK_CG=512 (one group at a time per program) is fine, but reducing across all 16 groups in one persistent row-program improves L1/L2 reuse of gamma/beta and lets the hardtanh epilogue ship the row without a second load.
